run_card.name: gems58-ribbon-sigma-adaptive-40768-20261011T052942Z
run_card.hypothesis: H58-R2 ribbon lane: with the localisation error sigma(x) measured on a buffered hide-and-recover holdout and cross-fitted leave-one-block-out, the exact-metric-optimal emission is a per-segment ribbon of parallel dotted lines on the kernel-radius lattice, not a single tight line and not a fixed-width ribbon.
run_card.mechanism: the scoring kernel is isotropic with R = 300 m, so a detected ridge that is off by sigma only earns credit where a parallel line falls inside 300 m of the true trace; lines at 0, +-3, +-6 px convert a multi-pixel localisation error into kernel credit at a cost of exactly alpha = 0.2 per emitted pixel
run_card.named_non_fault_process: aeromagnetic flight-line levelling and draped-sensor artefacts produce lineaments parallel to survey lines that no fault occupies; dense volcanic and alluvial contacts in the detrended DEM produce scarp-shaped curvature that is not tectonic
run_card.holdout_dti_evaluator: gems58w.metric/v1 (exact triangular kernel, R=3 px, alpha=0.2, beta=0.8)

holdout_dti_ci.note: min-max over the four spatial blocks. A bootstrap over 4 blocks resamples repeated physical blocks as independent, so no bootstrap CI is reported (the defect the previous instrument had).

local_screen.definitions: forward_overlap = fraction of MY dots within 3 px of the witness's dots (gems57.uniqueness.dot_overlap); reverse_overlap = fraction of the witness's dots within 3 px of mine; E = fraction of the footprint within 3 px of the witness's dots; lift = (observed - E) / (1 - E).

registry.note: the full 694/695-raster public inventory scan is run separately by scripts/check_uniqueness_registry.py; its verdict governs

run_card.submission_note: Ribbon lane: adaptive dotted ribbons 0/+-300/+-600 m on catalogue-free Hessian ridges (sigma cross-fitted); 40768 isolated dots at 1.0.
run_card.verdict_reason: The protocol's literal stop rule fired: 81 of 702 byte-verified inventory witnesses have more than 70 % of this file's dots within 3 px of theirs (54 of those firings are against witnesses whose chance-level expected overlap E >= 0.99 and are therefore information-free, and 27 are against broad dot fields of 155,021-3,380,827 dots). By the standing instruction the lane logs this as a duplicate and stops. Every discriminating statistic passes by a wide margin: byte-unique, pixel-unique, worst rank correlation 0.1824 (limit 0.90, 0 firings), worst dot-set Jaccard 0.1041 (limit 0.50, 0 firings), and no witness whose own expected overlap is below 0.30 exceeds 0.6115, and under a lift rule (observed - E)/(1 - E) > 0.50 the only 2 firings are this repository's own earlier ribbon files, the highest lift against any other repository being 0.4898. The file is therefore a reviewable artifact, not a cleared submission, and the open item is the owner's protocol decision recorded on the site.

site_gates.name: Uniqueness — chance-corrected reading (needs owner ratification)
site_gates.detail: Worst forward overlap against a witness that could have failed to fire: 0.8750 (13GEMSDOE:docs/downloads/archive/13gems-composite-20260929T183221Z_allfinite.tif), whose own chance-level expectation is E = 0.8611, so the chance-corrected lift is only 0.543 against this repo's own control file and 0.375 at most among the firings. The file is unique in every discriminating sense (bytes, pixels, rank order, dot-set Jaccard) and the firings are all against near-plane-filling witnesses — but this reading is not the protocol as written, so it is reported as an open owner decision and never as a pass.

live_evidence.verdict_note: The two-parameter catalogue-proximity model does not explain the owner-quoted live scores of 66 sha256-verified rasters (R^2 < 0, Spearman ~ 0), and no dot-field summary statistic reaches |Spearman| 0.30. Two organizer-confirmed facts explain why the evidence is this weak: (1) the public leaderboard pools only an undisclosed public subset of the region (thread 11550, 'We are not providing any information on the chunking / subsets'), so each quoted score carries chunk-luck noise we cannot model; (2) the Initial Prize Round is scored on the private subset, which no quoted score here measures. Consequence for the lane: the emission rule cannot be calibrated from live evidence, so it is set by the exact-metric marginal-inclusion bar and by the holdout-measured sigma, and no projection is written as a score.

irregularities.text: The owner's stated target 0.3195 is stale. The live public leaderboard (fetched 2026-10-11) has 0.4133 — xiaofanhu (public leaderboard #1, fetched 2026-10-11) at #1, and 0.3195 (DARD) at #8. Every 'beat the target' statement on this site is restated against 0.4133. leaderboard

The 19-band training_features.tif has no aeroradiometric bands (no eK/eU/eTh/total count) although the competition's own About page says GeoDAWN acquired aeromagnetic and aeroradiometric surveys plus 3DEP lidar. The radiometric signature of K-metasomatism, silicification and Fe-oxide staining — a physically motivated discriminator for faults hidden under cover — is therefore unreachable from the provided stack, and the USGS release is not fetchable from this sandbox (text-only egress). Recorded as an owner-download idea with verified links, never as a validated candidate. About page · USGS GeoDAWN

Shared-tool bug, fixed once in the template. src/gems58w/uniqueness.py computed the protocol's forward statistic — the fraction of my dots within 3 px of the witness's dots — in the reverse direction and vice versa, and applied the dense-prior exemption to the wrong leg. Every overlap number this lane published before 2026-10-11, including the '0.3600 worst forward overlap' quoted for the earlier 38,000-dot file, was measured with the two directions exchanged and has been re-measured with the corrected instrument. The template-level registry scanner (scripts/check_uniqueness_registry.py) already had the direction right, so the frozen-inventory numbers published by the sibling lane were unaffected.

The literal 0.70 overlap gate is unusable as written. Lattice and blanket witnesses dilate to cover 74–99.9 % of the footprint, so their chance-level expected overlap E exceeds 0.99 and they overlap every nonempty candidate; a literal firing against such a witness carries no information, and no buffer from 3 to 10 px clears 0.70 against them (measured in evidence/buffer_overlap_scan.json). The instrument now reports E, the chance-corrected lift (observed − E)/(1 − E), a saturated flag and an informative reading that excludes saturated witnesses, with the literal reading still reported alongside it.

The scanner rejected the organizer's own submission representation. sample_submission.tif carries NaN outside the study footprint (nodata=nan, 7,111,787 pixels) and finite values inside it, but the uniqueness scanner demanded an all-finite candidate, which is why earlier artifacts had to be published as *-zeros.tif variants that do not match the official representation. Fixed once in the shared tool: non-finite inside the footprint stays a hard error (that is exactly the portal rejection Predicted values must be in range [0, 1]), non-finite outside it is normalised to 0 for statistics that are footprint-restricted anyway.

The mandated holdout cannot score an off-catalogue file. The withheld truth is catalogue, so a candidate that keeps a 3 px catalogue margin scores HOLDOUT-DTI exactly 0.0 by construction (control raster sha256 53496109…, evidence/ribbon/instrument_control.json). The delivered file therefore drops only the dots that fall on the catalogue — which the organizer masks out of evaluation anyway — and reports a genuine non-zero HOLDOUT-DTI. That number measures catalogue recovery, not new-fault detection. staff answer on masking

No dot-field statistic predicts the owner-quoted live scores. Over 66 sha256-verified sibling rasters the best covariate reaches |Spearman| 0.258 and the two-parameter catalogue-proximity model fits with R² = −1.27. The organizer will not disclose public-subset membership, so every owner-quoted score carries unmodellable chunk luck. This file's budget is therefore taken from the measured family (median dot count of the owner-reported ≥0.24 files) and labelled USER-REPORTED-SCORE, never as a calibrated optimum. staff answer on pooling

The lane's 'single tight line where σ < 0.5 px' branch is unreachable: gems58w.sigma floors σ at 0.5 px and every measured stratum sits far above it (pooled median σ ≈ 6.88 px, block medians 5.79–8.54 px). The adaptive planner consequently returns 5 lines for most segments; the ribbon is never chosen because σ is small anywhere. The measured adaptivity is therefore 'ribbon vs tight line' more than 'per-segment line count'.

The sibling lane's published clearance is the reverse statistic. docs/deliverable/downloads/gems58-novel-scatter-44090-20261011T0630Z.tif is offered with a green banner on the strength of “worst 3 px forward overlap 0.3160 · 0 triggers” over 473 rasters. Re-measured in the protocol direction against the same byte-verified inventory it has 78 firings (worst 1.0000 against a plane-filling witness) and 0 in the reverse direction — the signature of the exchanged-directions bug (IR-58-UNIQ-04) that this session fixed in the shared tool. Not an accusation of duplication: the same degeneracy fires 81 times on this session's candidate. The irregularity is that the two lanes report opposite verdicts from the same registry because they measured different statistics, and that the two inventories are not the same set (473 live-fetched vs 703 pinned+delta). evidence/ribbon/sibling_direction_check.json

The pinned inventory was one raster short, and is now complete. The 695-raster public inventory could not be fully restored earlier because one file (sha256 927dc17f…) only existed in a deleted pull-request head. It was recovered by fetching the exact commit d92606c28dc5e93ee1bce5148b92ccbb5225d023 of 55GEMSDOE over the git protocol and verifying the blob's sha256, so the scan now covers 695/695 pinned rasters plus a freshness delta from the current default branches.
